notable_absence.finding: Table 1 (Configuration Levels) suffered a markdown-conversion defect: several 'Changeable?' cells are corrupted merges of two sentences with no separating punctuation or whitespace, e.g. 'Yes, file-editRestart required' and 'Yes by the Admin REST APINo restart, but **not persisted**'. The restart/persistence axis for Node, System properties, Logging properties, Database and Replication properties levels is present in the source but not cleanly machine-extractable from this snapshot without consulting the original AsciiDoc; relations 8 and 9 above were built instead from clean prose sentences elsewhere on the page that make the same two points (manual restart for bootstrap/node config vs. automatic restart for persistent/database config).

cross_component_finding: This page names three superficially similar collective nouns - 'Sync Gateway Cluster', 'Homogeneous Sync Gateway Cluster', and 'Sync Gateway Config Group' - in a single three-row Key Terms table, distinguishing a cluster (any nodes sharing one Couchbase Server cluster), a homogeneous cluster (a cluster where every node shares config), and a config group (a named subset of a cluster's nodes sharing config, the general case of which a homogeneous cluster is the trivial one-group instance). Only sgw:config-group and sgw:sync-gateway-cluster were minted as concepts here since they are the two structurally distinct entities; 'Homogeneous Sync Gateway Cluster' is a degenerate case of the config-group mechanism (a cluster with exactly one, default, all-encompassing group) rather than a third structure, so minting it separately was judged to add a label without a new mechanism.
cross_product_finding: The Eventing Service dependency (service:eventing-service requiresSetting sgw:persistent-configuration) is the first concrete, source-stated coupling this round has found between Sync Gateway's own configuration mode and a Couchbase Server-side service's ability to function correctly - Eventing silently loses compatibility-check visibility into databases created under legacy file-based config because they are 'not recorded in the registry'. This is a genuine cross-product finding distinct from the two disjoint-identity-system findings established in round 3 (sgw:rbac-user vs sgw:user) and the TLS-transport-layer finding in secure-sgw-access.json: it shows Sync Gateway's internal configuration-mode choice reaching outward to affect a Couchbase Server feature's own behaviour, not merely reusing a Couchbase Server identity or transport mechanism.
